comparator.name: Nutrition and Health
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: 121 EC of positive-credit compulsory common study (plus two zero-credit safety requirements), a 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, a 12-EC bachelor thesis and 44 EC of open electives. A zero-minimum skills option does not add credit to the selected pathway, and the optional 6-EC lab-based thesis extension is not selected. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected by the official-order tie-break.
components: Nutrition and Health: Macronutrients, Energy and Health
Introduction to the Field of Nutrition and Health
General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Introduction to Epidemiology and Public Health
Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms for Health
Research Methodology for Nutrition and Health I
Research Methodology for Nutrition and Health II
Selected by official-order tie-break from the 3-EC mathematics/statistics restricted choice.
The optional 6-EC lab-based thesis extension is not selected in this coherent 180-EC pathway.
Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

alternatives.label: Nutrition, physiology, behaviour & population health
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum connects molecular and cellular life science, physiology and metabolism with epidemiology, behaviour, public health, statistics and research.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible nutrition-and-health response spanning molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, disease, epidemiology, eating and health behaviour, population health and mixed research methods.
progression: Life-science, public-health, psychology, sociology, data and research foundations precede physiology, biochemistry, laboratory research, genetics, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, health psychology and communication. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Molecular nutrition, metabolism & disease
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and laboratory research.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced biomedical-nutrition direction through molecular and cell biology, metabolism-related biochemistry, physiology, genetics, pharmacology, infection, immunity and disease mechanisms.
progression: Life-science, physiology, biochemistry, statistics and laboratory foundations precede molecular pathology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and advanced biomedical research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This direction replaces much of the closest programme’s sociology, qualitative methods, behaviour, communication and population-health breadth with deeper molecular, biomedical, neuroscience and translational study. It differs by at least four courses and 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Nutrition behaviour, public health & communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres epidemiology, psychology, sociology, food and health behaviour, population prevention and communication.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced behavioural and population-nutrition direction through epidemiology, psychology, sociology, health behaviour, communication, public health and prevention research.
progression: Public-health, life-science, psychology, communication, sociology and data foundations precede health psychology, behaviour-focused persuasion, disease mechanisms and applied communication. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This direction makes eating and health behaviour, psychology, population prevention and communication the organising priority. It differs from both the integrated closest programme and the molecular direction by well over four courses and 30 EC.

core: Human nutrition, dietary requirements, digestion and health
Molecular and cellular biology, physiology, metabolism and disease
Eating behaviour, social influences, sensory science and communication
Epidemiology, public health, prevention and population evidence
Statistics, dietary measurement, data analysis and independent nutrition research
adjacent: Nutrition behaviour, epidemiology and public-health communication
questions: How do nutrients, digestion, metabolism and physiology shape health and disease?
How can molecular and biomedical evidence evaluate nutritional effects and health claims?
How do behaviour, society and population evidence inform nutrition and disease prevention?

selection.assessment: The integrated closest programme spans biology, physiology, behaviour and population health. Biomedical nutrition/metabolism and behavioural-population nutrition each support coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct additional directions. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR provides a dedicated nutrition curriculum from macronutrients, digestion and metabolism through food technology, sensory science, dietary-intake measurement, nutritional epidemiology, two nutrition-specific research-methods courses and a nutrition thesis. UCR can combine substantial biomedical science, physiology, psychology, epidemiology, public health, data and communication, but does not reproduce that specialist nutrition sequence course for course.
